title: Farkas Lemma
body_html:
Farkas Lemma

Let $A$ be an $m\times n$ real matrix, $b\in\mathbb R^m$, $c\in\mathbb R^n$, and $d\in\mathbb R$. Assume $$ S=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\ge b\} $$ is nonempty. Then the following are equivalent:

  1. for every $x\in\mathbb R^n$, if $Ax\ge b$ then $\langle c,x\rangle\ge d$;
  2. there exists $u\in\mathbb R^m$ such that $u\ge 0$, $uA=c$, and $\langle u,b\rangle\ge d$.

References

  • [MFoGT, Section 2.8, Exercise 8] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory, references/MathFoundationsGameTheory.pdf. Farkas lemma derived from the theorem of the alternative.
